clue.text: Guaranteeing NHS success in the Home Counties?

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
a success for the National Health Service is curing a patient

explanation.surface: A question about whether the health service does well in the commuter counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London; the NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Securing a deal means making it certain, so it is a synonym for guaranteeing.

clue.text: Greek poet's brief attempt to embrace software

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside, so the software term goes within the shortened attempt
brief means cut short, so the final letter of the word for attempt is dropped

parts.note: an attempt is a shot, as in having a shot at something
an app is a piece of software

explanation.surface: A poet makes a quick try at handling a computer program.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was the lyric poet of ancient Lesbos, a Greek writer of the sixth century BC.

clue.text: Picked up remaining eggs

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for remaining is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: remaining means over, as in food left over

explanation.surface: Someone collects the eggs that are left.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent OVER and OVA sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the Latin plural for egg cells, the female reproductive cells.

clue.text: Brunch is half finished, and the cat's chewed one of the canapés

indicators.note: a word half finished keeps only its first half, here the opening three of its six letters
chewed means mangled, so the letters of the cat's are rearranged

explanation.surface: Brunch is half eaten and the cat has gnawed one of the party nibbles.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'cat's' is ignored, as punctuation always is in anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruschetta is toasted bread with toppings, an Italian appetiser served as a canapé.

clue.text: Mention a false notion, one initially ignored

indicators.note: initially ignored means the letter for one is dropped from the front

parts.note: a false notion is an illusion
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone raises a mistaken idea while one point is passed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a false notion' looks like anagram material, but it is A plus ILLUSION, whose opening I (one) goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An allusion is an indirect reference, so it is a passing mention of something.

clue.text: Neglected newspaper needs good editor

parts.note: a rag is a slang word for a newspaper, especially a poor one

explanation.surface: A paper that has been let go needs a capable editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ragged is worn and shabby, as a neglected garment or garden would be.

clue.text: Enjoys hot dish

parts.note: to enjoy something is to have it, as in having a good time
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone likes a spicy meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash is a dish of chopped meat and potato fried together.

clue.text: Raise capital for writer

parts.note: to jack up a car is to raise it
London is the capital of the UK

explanation.surface: A call to gather funds for an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise capital' reads as fundraising; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack London was the American novelist who wrote The Call of the Wild.

clue.text: Seedy dive's opening next to a new hotel, unfortunately

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters of a new hotel are jumbled

explanation.surface: A shabby bar has unhappily opened beside a newly built hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dive' looks like a swimming plunge but is a sleazy bar; only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Down-at-heel describes something shabby and run-down, which is what seedy means.

clue.text: A singer performing

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird, so a singer in crossword terms

explanation.surface: A vocalist on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' looks like a person but is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at it is an idiom for being busy doing something, so carrying on or performing.

clue.text: Works installing power in East London buildings?

indicators.note: installing means putting in, so the power letter goes inside

parts.note: in the Cockney speech of East London houses drops its H, giving 'ouses

explanation.surface: Construction jobs fitting electricity into homes in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney, the East London accent, drops the H from houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Opuses are musical or literary compositions, plural of opus, a creative work.

clue.text: Small child who can't yet walk and who writes badly?

definitions.note: stands for a person who writes badly

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
a baby that cannot walk yet moves about as a crawler

explanation.surface: A toddler not yet on their feet who also has poor handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawler produces untidy, careless handwriting, so is someone with poor penmanship.

clue.text: Support military commander with inside information

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: inside means the word for with goes within the commander's title

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander
with means and, as in bread with butter

explanation.surface: Backing a general who has secret intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside information' looks like one phrase; 'inside' is the container signal and 'information' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is biased information spread to promote a cause.

clue.text: Change of heart for everyone in trouble

indicators.note: a change of heart swaps the central letter of the word for everyone for another

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone's mind changes while they are in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of heart' swaps the middle L of ALL for an I.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to trouble or afflict, as in what ails you.

clue.text: Touring eastern part of Commonwealth, children showing excitement

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word for children surrounds the other letters

parts.note: fry are young fish, hence small children
New Zealand, NZ, is a member of the Commonwealth

explanation.surface: Children on a trip through the eastern Commonwealth get worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A frenzy is a state of wild excitement or agitation.

clue.text: Flapping wings, say, insect gets about

indicators.note: gets about means goes around, so the insect surrounds the word for say

parts.note: a fly is an insect
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: An insect beating its wings, for instance, moves around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the 'for example' marker after 'Flapping wings'; it is UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluttery describes something that flutters, moving its wings in quick light beats.

clue.text: Stood in tempest without raincoat at first, and suffered

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed from the storm

parts.note: a tempest is a storm

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: ached means suffered pain

explanation.surface: Someone stood out in a storm without a coat and paid for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffered' looks like the definition, but it is ACHED; 'Stood' in the sense of tolerated is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stomached something is to have put up with it, as one stood a nuisance.

clue.text: White wine — drink heralding unlimited happiness

indicators.note: heralding means coming before, so the drink is placed first

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

indicators.note: unlimited means without a limit, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: bliss is great happiness

explanation.surface: A white wine as the drink that brings boundless joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white Burgundy made from Chardonnay grapes.

clue.text: Sturdy old boy goes into decline

indicators.note: goes into means is put inside the word for decline

parts.note: to rust is to decline or deteriorate through neglect
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A tough former pupil goes downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means strong and healthy, a synonym for sturdy.

clue.text: Nervy type's new way to save money

indicators.note: to save is to keep in, so the money goes inside

parts.note: a path is a way
the euro is a currency

explanation.surface: A jittery person finds a fresh way of saving cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuropath is a person with a nervous disorder, so is literally a nervy type.

clue.text: Son and friend welcoming that girl round

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the girl goes inside

parts.note: a pal is a friend
her is the pronoun for that girl

explanation.surface: A son and his mate greet a girl who visits.
explanation.definitionFit: Spheral means shaped like a sphere, so round or globular.

clue.text: Old reservists travel in endless fear over a South American region

indicators.note: over in a down clue means placed above the next piece
in means put inside the shortened fear
endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: panic is sudden fear
TA is the Territorial Army, the British Army's former name for its volunteer reserve
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Former reservists journey in constant dread to a part of South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims PANIC to PANI, into which TA GO goes; 'over' sets A beneath in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagonia is the region at the southern tip of South America, shared by Argentina and Chile.

clue.text: Sacking to lift over top of house

indicators.note: in a down clue over the top of means set above, so the lift comes first

parts.note: to heave is to lift something heavy

explanation.surface: A sack to be hoisted over the roof of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacking' looks like a material; it means dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the heave-ho means being dismissed, so it is an informal word for sacking.

clue.text: Teacher's words to class, once question's been answered convincingly

definitions.text: Teacher's words to class, once question's been answered
definitions.meaning: a teacher tells raised arms to be lowered after a pupil has replied
means easily and decisively, as in winning without a contest

explanation.surface: A schoolroom moment after a pupil answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning by this margin is an idiom for winning easily, beyond doubt.

clue.text: Container boat reported first on a large European waterway

indicators.note: first means this piece comes before the rest
reported means spoken, so a word sounding like the boat word is used

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed boat, and poetically a ship
a can is a container

explanation.surface: A container ship heads a large shipping route in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kiel Canal crosses northern Germany, linking the North Sea and the Baltic.

clue.text: End of revolution followed by a gathering of workers, of course

indicators.note: followed by means the next pieces come after
the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: TU is a trade union, an organisation of workers
a rally is a mass gathering

explanation.surface: A revolution ends with a mass meeting of workers, as you would expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally and of course both say something is to be expected.

clue.text: In theory, journalist works here

definitions.meaning: means theoretically, as plans that look good but are untested
a reporter is employed at a newspaper

explanation.surface: Theoretically, this is where a reporter is employed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that works in principle is said to work this way, and a journalist writes for a paper.

clue.text: Tour oddly deficient, with no time for region of Italy

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word
with no means removing the time letter

parts.note: scanty means deficient or insufficient

explanation.surface: A trip falls short and runs out of time for a visit to Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no time' drops a T from SCANTY to give SCANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscany is the region of central Italy containing Florence.

clue.text: Wearing old-fashioned hat, internee cultivated land

indicators.note: wearing means having the hat around, so the hat letters enclose the internee

parts.note: tile is dated slang for a hat
a lag is a prisoner, as in old lag

explanation.surface: A prisoner in an old hat has farmed the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' looks like a verb but describes the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is land that has been ploughed and tilled for crops.

clue.text: Knowledgeable type reset satnav

indicators.note: reset means set again in another order, so the letters of the satnav are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever person resets the navigation device.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned person, a scholar of great knowledge.
